Before your shift

Getting started

This handbook covers the screens you'll use as the front-desk Receptionist: registering patients, booking and confirming appointments, and running today's queue. Every screenshot below is the real system, so what you see here is exactly what you'll see on your screen.

  1. 1Open the hospital system in your browser and go to the address given to you by the Admin team.
  2. 2Type the Username and Password your Admin created for you.
  3. 3Click Login. You will land on your Receptionist Dashboard automatically — no need to pick a role.
🔒Forgot your password? Only an Admin can reset it for you — ask them directly, the screen itself has no "forgot password" link.
👁 What you'll see — the login screen, in front of a photo of the medical centre building.

Status colours at a glance

Every appointment carries a coloured label. Learn these five and the rest of the system reads itself.

booked — patient booked online, not yet confirmed
confirmed — arrival confirmed, waiting to check in
checked_in — ready and waiting for the doctor
no_show — patient did not arrive
cancelled — appointment called off
1

Register a patient

Do this for every walk-in who is not already in the system — a new student, staff member, or guest.

  1. 1Click Register Patient in the left menu.
  2. 2Choose Student & Visitors or Faculty & Staff, whichever fits the person in front of you.
  3. 3Fill in their Patient Type, name, ID, email, date of birth, gender, contact number and address/hostel exactly as they tell you.
  4. 4Click Complete Registration.
  5. 5A green banner confirms success and shows their new Institute ID — note this down if they ask for it.
Step 2 — pick the registration type
Step 3 — the form, filled in
Step 5 — success, and the system immediately asks if you want to book their appointment
2

Book an appointment

Straight after registering, or any time from the Patient Directory's Book button.

  1. 1Click Yes, book appointment on the prompt.
  2. 2Under Doctors Available Today, find the right doctor and click Book Now on their card.
  3. 3The next screen shows the doctor, date and a suggested Time Slot — change the slot if needed.
  4. 4Click Confirm & Book. The patient now appears in today's queue as confirmed.
Step 2 — only doctors on duty today are shown
Step 3 — confirm the time slot
💡No doctor listed today? Use Schedule for a Later Date at the bottom of the booking screen instead.
3

Today's queue

Booked Appointments in the left menu — your main screen for the day.

  1. 1Appointments patients booked themselves online appear under Booked Appointments first.
  2. 2Appointments you booked at the desk appear straight under Confirmed Appointments.
  3. 3Use the Start Date / End Date boxes and the Status drop-down to look at a different day.
  4. 4Click Refresh any time to pull the latest list.
A confirmed appointment, with its Check-in and No Show buttons on the right
4

Check a patient in

Once the patient has physically arrived and is ready to see the doctor.

  1. 1Find their row in Confirmed Appointments.
  2. 2Click the green Check-in button.
  3. 3Their status changes to checked_in and their OPD slip opens automatically.
  4. 4Click Print Prescription to hand them a printed slip, or Close if it isn't needed yet.
The confirmation toast, with the OPD slip ready to print
⚠Patient never arrived? Click No Show instead of leaving them unchecked — it keeps the doctor's queue accurate.
5

Find a patient

Patient Directory in the left menu — every patient ever registered, in one searchable list.

  1. 1Type a name, Institute ID, or contact number into the search box.
  2. 2Use All Doctors to narrow results to one doctor's patients.
  3. 3Click Book on a row to start a new appointment for that patient.
  4. 4Not sure what a status badge means? Click Status Guide, top right.
Search, filter, and book — all from one list
6

Appointment history

A record of past appointments — useful when a patient asks "when did I last visit?"

  1. 1Click Appointment History in the left menu.
  2. 2Set a date range and, optionally, a status, then click Refresh.
Filter by date range and status
7

Doctor schedule

Visiting Doctor Schedule — check who is on duty, and when, before you book.

  1. 1Search a doctor by name or department, or scroll the full list.
  2. 2Switch to Calendar View for a week-at-a-glance layout.
Each doctor's weekly duty hours
8

Doctor leaves

Manage Doctor Leaves — mark a doctor unavailable so patients aren't booked into an empty room.

  1. 1Choose the doctor from Select Doctor.
  2. 2Set the Start Date and End Date of their leave.
  3. 3Add a short reason, e.g. "Health checkup".
  4. 4Click Mark Doctor On Leave. It now appears in the Leave Records List on the right.
Recording a leave keeps the booking screen accurate

Getting help

If a screen on your computer looks different from this guide, or an action here doesn't work the way it's described, do not guess — contact your Admin or IT support before continuing. This guide was captured directly from the system on 8 September 2026 using a training patient record; nothing here is a real patient's data.
